### 1. Scene
A mixed buffet-style plate: an apple, a fresh spring roll, several cooked meats, and a small portion of roasted vegetables or crispy trimmings. Meat identification is somewhat uncertain.

### 2. Vessel
A white dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3–7. Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Areas below represent non-overlapping food footprints. The exposed central bone is excluded from the edible-meat estimate. No separate oil or sauce is clearly visible; cooking fat is included in the calorie densities.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × average height = volume | Density → grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| Whole apple | 7% | 37 × 4 = 148 ml | 0.85 → **126 g** | 52 | 66 |
| Fresh vegetable/shrimp spring roll | 5% | 27 × 2 = 54 ml | 0.85 → **46 g** | 110 | 51 |
| Central bone-in roasted meat, likely poultry; edible portion only | 13% | 69 × 1.7 = 117 ml | 0.95 → **111 g** | 200 | 222 |
| Dark roasted meat at right, possibly pork | 7% | 37 × 1.8 = 67 ml | 0.95 → **64 g** | 290 | 186 |
| Roasted vegetables/crispy trimmings at top | 4% | 21 × 1.2 = 25 ml | 0.85 → **21 g** | 180 | 38 |
| Skin-on roasted chicken piece at left | 6% | 32 × 1.7 = 54 ml | 0.95 → **51 g** | 250 | 128 |
| Small white chicken-meat strips at bottom | 3% | 16 × 0.8 = 13 ml | 0.95 → **12 g** | 165 | 20 |

### 8. Sanity check
The food footprints total **45% of the plate**, with additional space occupied by the exposed bone. The estimated **431 g of edible food and 711 kcal** is plausible for the visible apple, small roll, and assorted meat portions. The greatest uncertainty is the identity and fat content of the roasted meats.
